We want to understand what you meant by "there was something near the bottom of the screen, some kind of action I think, though I couldn't quite tell what it was for", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The large “Continue Shopping” bar near the bottom, which appears more prominent than the order placement area below it.

B) The grey “Place Order” bar beneath “Continue Shopping,” which appears visually muted and somewhat buried near the bottom.

C) The small legal/privacy text at the very bottom, which sits below the main action areas and may make the lower section feel unclear.

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
turns.a: If I had to pick... probably B? I think. Though I'm not sure that's exactly it — it might be closer to another option, depending on how you're defining it. It's more of a general feeling than a specific thing. Other people might not even notice.

turns.q: What kind of shopping or ordering situation would bring you to review a layout where a grey “Place Order” bar sits below “Continue Shopping”?
turns.a: I'm not sure I have one specific moment in mind. It's more of a... recurring thing, I suppose. When the team needs to process something quickly and there's not much time for setup. Though I'm not sure that's specific enough.

turns.q: When you noticed the muted “Place Order” bar under “Continue Shopping,” what were you trying to verify about the ordering options visible on that screen?
turns.a: I suppose just... complete the transaction. Get it submitted. I don't usually think of it as a 'job' — it's more like a step in something larger. Someone else usually handles the follow-up.

turns.q: What would “working well” look like for the grey “Place Order” bar so it clearly supports submitting the order without feeling buried under “Continue Shopping”?
turns.a: I'd know it worked if... nothing went wrong, I suppose. If a confirmation appeared and nothing needed to be corrected. That's what success looks like for this kind of thing.

turns.q: What is it about the grey “Place Order” bar’s appearance — its fill, color, contrast, border, or label style — that makes it feel muted rather than like the primary action?
turns.a: The problem is visibility, really. The button to submit — the 'Place Order' button — didn't look like a primary action. It looked like a label. So I spent time looking for something that was already there, just... not visible enough.

turns.q: Looking directly at the grey “Place Order” bar, is the problem more that it has too little solid fill, that the grey color is too muted, or that the contrast against the surrounding area is too low?
turns.a: The button was gray on a gray background with very small text — 12 pixels, I think. For the primary action on the screen, that's basically invisible. I couldn't tell if it was meant to be interactive, if it was disabled, or if I was just overlooking it. The barrier is the contrast. To remove it: give the 'Place Order' button a solid fill color that actually stands out from the background, and increase the text to something legible — 16 pixels minimum. That's the change. Everything else on the screen was fine.
